Its LabRobFail-Data dataset organizes failures into five major categories: Perception, Grasping, Motion, Logic, and Safety, with 11 fine-grained failure types. LabRobFail-Bench evaluates failure understanding across multiple dimensions: detecting whether a failure occurred, locating it temporally, classifying its mode, assessing severity, and planning precise corrective actions. The associated simulation framework, LabRobFail-Sim, generates failures through controllable perturbations at three levels. Control-level perturbations model execution and actuator faults, including pose noise and gripper-command corruption. Physics-level perturbations alter properties such as friction, mass, and viscosity to produce slippage or grasp instability. Semantic-level perturbations introduce workflow and logic errors, including reversing or skipping steps and substituting target objects such as reagents, potentially violating safety constraints. The framework emphasizes actionable, risk-aware diagnosis and recovery rather than binary detection or ambiguous corrective feedback.
